rules.title: Cartwright Act: common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of an unlawful restraint of trade, or coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or term, is prohibited. This is not a blanket prohibition on every pricing tool.
rules.requirement_es: Se prohíbe usar o distribuir un algoritmo común de precios como parte de una restricción ilícita del comercio, o coaccionar a otra persona para adoptar sus recomendaciones. No es una prohibición general de toda herramienta de precios.
rules.quoted_span:

(b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Covered continuing tenancies are limited to the lower of 5% plus regional CPI or 10% over 12 months, with no more than two increases; initial rent after all prior tenants leave, statutory exemptions and stronger local controls require separate review. Excess-rent demands or collections can lead to excess-rent damages, injunctions and discretionary fees; willful conduct, oppression, fraud or malice can support damages up to three times the excess rent.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendamientos continuos cubiertos tienen un límite de 12 meses equivalente al menor valor entre el 5% más el IPC regional y el 10%, con un máximo de dos aumentos; el alquiler inicial tras la salida de todos los inquilinos, las exenciones y los controles locales más protectores requieren revisión aparte. Exigir o cobrar alquiler excesivo puede dar lugar a daños por el exceso, medidas judiciales y honorarios discrecionales; la conducta deliberada, opresiva, fraudulenta o maliciosa puede justificar daños de hasta tres veces el exceso.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause
rules.requirement: Covered tenancies require stated just cause after every tenant has continuously occupied for at least 12 months or one tenant for at least 24 months; a qualifying no-fault termination also requires one month of relocation assistance or a final-month rent waiver. Noncompliance voids the termination notice; materially unlawful attempts to recover possession can lead to actual damages, discretionary fees, and, for willfulness, oppression, fraud or malice, up to three times actual damages and possible punitive damages.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendamientos cubiertos requieren causa justificada cuando todos los inquilinos llevan al menos 12 meses o uno lleva al menos 24 meses; una terminación sin culpa que reúna los requisitos también exige ayuda de un mes o la exención del último mes de alquiler. El incumplimiento invalida el aviso de terminación; los intentos de recuperar la posesión en infracción sustancial pueden generar daños reales y honorarios discrecionales, y, si existe conducta deliberada, opresiva, fraudulenta o maliciosa, hasta tres veces los daños reales y posibles daños punitivos.
rules.key_value: 12 months all tenants / 24 months one tenant
rules.exemptions: See Civil Code § 1946.2(e), including transient occupancy, care facilities, dormitories, shared owner facilities, qualifying owner occupancy, new construction and restricted affordable housing; qualifying local just-cause ordinances govern instead.

rules.title: Standard security deposit ceiling
rules.requirement: For security newly collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024, the ordinary ceiling is one month of rent, excluding the first month; the qualifying small-landlord exception, advance-rent provision and requested-alteration provision require separate review. Bad-faith claims or retention of security can result in actual damages plus statutory damages up to twice the security.

Reclamar o retener la fianza de mala fe puede generar daños reales más una indemnización legal de hasta el doble de la fianza.

rules.title: No discrimination based on lawful income source
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not discriminate based on a protected characteristic, including lawful source of income; subsidized-housing criteria must use the tenant-paid rent portion and offer qualifying alternative ability-to-pay evidence in place of credit history. Available discrimination remedies include out-of-pocket and emotional-distress damages, access to denied housing, injunctions, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.

Entre los posibles remedios por discriminación figuran pérdidas económicas, acceso a la vivienda denegada, daños emocionales, medidas judiciales, sanciones civiles o daños punitivos y honorarios de abogado.

rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in rental advertising, applications, selection or decisions except within limited exceptions, and criminal-history action requires written notice and an opportunity to respond. rules.title: Coordinated rental pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Selling or using coordinated pricing algorithms that use recent nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy for Berkeley homes is prohibited, subject to defined research, aggregated-reporting and affordable-housing exclusions. Civil penalties may reach $1,000 per violation, with each month and dwelling unit counted separately for landlord use; the City Attorney may sue over sale or use and an aggrieved tenant over use, with damages, injunctions and prevailing-party fees available.

Las sanciones civiles pueden llegar a 1.000 dólares por infracción, contando por separado cada mes y vivienda en el uso por el propietario; la Abogacía de la Ciudad puede demandar por venta o uso y un inquilino afectado por uso, con daños, medidas judiciales y honorarios para la parte vencedora.

A. “Coordinated pricing algorithm” means any analytical or computation process that 
uses Competitor Data to calculate and recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates or 
other rental contract terms for future leases in coordination between one City of Berkeley 
landlord and one or more of such landlord’s competitors, including through a third-party 
vendor.

does not include (a) a product or process that 
generates or presents any report, study, or presentation that publishes rental data in an 
aggregated and anonymous manner but does not recommend rent prices, fees, or 
occupancy rates or other rental contract terms for future leases; (b) a product used for 
the purpose of establishing rent or income limits in accordance with the affordable 
housing guidelines of a local government, the state, the federal government, or other 
political subdivision; or (c) a product or process that provides or uses, or the provision or 
use of, information for the purpose of (i) conducting market research for project financing,

development. For clarity, “research, testing, or training for software development” 
includes without limitation the use or processing of Competitor Data in the development, 
training, or testing of predictive or machine learning models so long as any such data is 
not used as an input in the operation of the model at the time a recommendation is

than 90 days old.

in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

§98.0704 Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy

Tenancy means the lawful right or entitlement of a tenant to continuously use or 
occupy a residential rental property for more than 30 days. A tenancy does not 
include a lease for a fixed-term of three months or less, including any extensions or 
renewals of that lease for a fixed-term of three months or less.

§98.0709 Remedies 
(a) A tenant claiming a violation of this Division may file an action against a 
landlord in a court of competent jurisdiction. 
 
(b) A tenant may seek injunctive relief, equitable relief, and money damages, 
including punitive damages, in a civil action against a landlord for a violation 
of this Division.

(c) A tenant may raise, as an affirmative defense, any violation or noncompliance 
with this Division in any action by a landlord to recover possession of a 
residential rental property. 
 
(d) Any attempt by a landlord to recover possession of a residential rental 
property or any actual recovery of possession of a residential rental property 
in violation of this Division shall render the landlord liable to the tenant in a 
civil action for wrongful eviction for damages of not less than three times the 
actual economic damages.

(f) In the court's discretion, a landlord who attempts to recover possession of a 
residential rental property in material violation of this Division shall be liable 
to the tenant in a civil action for reasonable attorney’s fees and costs. 
 
(g) The remedies under section 98.0709 are cumulative and may be used in 
addition to any other remedies in this Division or at law, statute, or ordinance. 
 
(h) The City may enforce this Division under Chapter 1, Article 2 of this Code, 
including civil and criminal remedies.

§98.0710 Failure to Comply with Division 
In addition to other remedies applicable to landlord’s failure to comply with this 
Division, a landlord’s failure to comply with any provision of this Division shall 
render void any notice of termination required by this Division.
